payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones in the edited image?
node.criteria: Compare the mug’s position with the headphones in the SOURCE and EDITED images. Fulfillment requires the mug to be positioned to the right of the headphones.
node.binding: SOURCE: the mug and headphones in the original image. EDITED: compare their positions to determine whether the mug is to the right of the headphones.
node.source_quote: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
node.aspect: Relative position of the mug and headphones
node.endpoint: The mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.
node.necessity: This relative placement is the requested edit.
node.zero_when: The mug has not moved to the right of the headphones; unrelated edits do not count.
node.half_when: The mug has moved toward the right of the headphones but is not yet positioned to their right, with a concrete remaining positional deficiency.
node.full_when: The mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.

node_traces.evidence: In the source, the blue mug is to the left of the headphones. In the edited image, a mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones, so the requested relative placement is achieved.

response.content: {"text":"The binding is too loose: it identifies objects by category and asks only whether “a mug” is right of the headphones. In the edited image there are multiple mug-like objects, while the original blue mug appears as a blurred blue remnant on the left; the clear mug on the right may be a duplicate/new object, not the original mug moved. This makes the trace’s confident full-pass claim unsupported and can explain the partial reference. Tighten the binding to track the source blue mug’s identity across images, and have the criterion distinguish movement of that object from duplication, replacement, or an unrelated mug appearing to the right. Require evidence for both identity/continuity and final relative position, while allowing a partial judgment only when the tracked mug shows concrete progress but has not reached the endpoint. The trace reports no transport, schema, or dependency failure, so investigate this as a visual binding/criterion issue rather than an execution failure."}
